ai.description: This lizard reaches 25 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct dark nuchal crest and a pale lateral stripe. A prominent white or yellow patch marks the corner of the mouth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Japalura major* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, prominent fold of skin across the throat (gular fold), which is absent in most similar agamid species.
ai.habitat: *Japalura major* inhabits temperate forests and shrublands in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Large Mountain Lizard is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on rocks or tree trunks to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Japalura major* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Japalura major* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, primarily across Arunachal Pradesh, India, at elevations ranging from approximately 1,500 to 2,500 meters.
